claims.statement: Quetelet published Sur l'homme 1835 in Paris Bachelier as two-volume work; revised as Physique sociale 1869
Quetelet combined astronomical measurement-error analogy with population and social statistics
Quetelet's l'homme moyen concept took group mean as representative type; this was disputed and influential
Historical Quetelet worked on births mortality and criminal court or social observation statistics
Later historiography traces effects of average-type and determinism on psychology and other fields
Astronomical repeated measurement errors and real between-person variation are not interchangeable
Modern sample 10,10,11,19,20,20 has mean 15 and population variance 22; no observation equals 15
Mean-minimizes sum of squared errors; pooled mean must weight groups by sample sizes
Identical group mean can conceal mixture bimodality and dispersion
Counts without denominators or changing reporting mechanisms cannot establish stable rates or causes
Descriptive mean and normative ideals or social determinism are different claims not justified by averages
